title: Outcome Marketplace: Prioritized Initiative Bidding and Stakeholder SLAs
creator: Ava Collins
description:
Problem: company-level prioritization is drifting toward highest-visibility tickets rather than highest-expected outcome. Cross-functional teams spend cycles negotiating priorities each quarter, which creates rework and unclear ownership.

Proposal: build an "Outcome Marketplace"—a lightweight prioritization and commitment surface where teams ‘bid’ capacity and outcomes against company-level objectives. Each initiative is represented as a timeboxed Outcome Contract: owner, requested capacity (FTEs / ops), expected impact (OKR contribution), SLA for delivery checkpoints, and risk level. Stakeholders (PM, Eng, Design, Sales, SRE) can accept, partially accept with conditional SLAs, or counter-bid. The marketplace enables transparent trade-offs, explicit escalation paths, and measurable commitment SLAs that feed into quarterly roadmap and release gates.

Scope (MVP):
- Outcome contract schema and submission form (Confluence + source of truth link)
- Lightweight bidding UI (Google Sheet template -> Redwood Console integration later)
- SLA templates (timebox, checkpoint cadence, rollback conditions)
- Decision rubric mapping bids to company-level OKR scoring
- Rollout playbook and stakeholder RACI

Why this is different: rather than a top-down prioritization memo, the marketplace forces cross-functional commitments and explicit trade-offs. It makes the cost of shifting priorities visible (who is taking capacity hit), and creates an auditable trail for retro and resource planning.
acceptance_criteria: Outcome contract template published and linked in company strategy Confluence
At least 12 initiatives submitted for Q2 via the marketplace template
Stakeholder approvals (PM/Eng/Design/Revenue/SRE) captured for 80% of submitted initiatives
Decision rubric applied to submitted initiatives and produced a prioritized list with clear trade-offs
One pilot team completes an Outcome Contract and reports checkpoint results at 30/60/90 days
success_metrics: % of quarter-forward capacity captured in Outcome Contracts >= 65%
Time spent in ad-hoc prioritization meetings reduced by 40% (tooling + SLAs)
Number of scope changes requiring exec escalation reduced by 50%
Stakeholder satisfaction (post-cycle survey) >= 8/10 for clarity of commitments
timeline: Week 1 (2026-03-16): Finalize schema, SLA templates, and decision rubric
Week 2 (2026-03-23): Publish Confluence page, share templates, host runbook demo
Week 3-4 (2026-03-30 to 2026-04-06): Intake window for initiative submissions (pilot + open)
Week 5 (2026-04-13): Review window, bids collected, rubric applied, prioritized backlog published
Week 6 (2026-04-20): Pilot Outcome Contract kickoffs and checkpoint scheduling
risks: Risk: Teams treat bidding as political — mitigation: rubric enforces quantifiable OKR contribution and cost estimates
Risk: Overhead > value (too many admin cycles) — mitigation: start with lightweight sheet and strict submission window; measure admin time
Risk: Enforcement of SLAs — mitigation: define clear rollback conditions and executive arbitration flow
Risk: Cross-team dependencies block accepted bids — mitigation: require dependency declaration and assign a dependency owner in contract
